The study assessed the bactericidal activity of three cutaneous/mucosal antiseptic solutions in the presence of interfering substances according to the NF EN 13727 European Standard. The results showed that only one solution, CB, demonstrated significant bactericidal activity against the test pathogens, even when present with interferences.

This finding indicates that CB may be a suitable choice for adjunctive treatment of skin and mucous membranes disorders, primarily those caused by bacterial infections or potentially superinfecting bacteria, in vitro. However, further studies are recommended to validate this result in current practice conditions.

The study suggests that the NF EN 13727 standard has been adapted to assess the bactericidal activity of these antiseptic solutions under various conditions, allowing for a better understanding of their efficacy. While the results indicate that CB is effective against certain pathogens, it's essential to consider other factors such as patient demographics, age, and underlying health conditions when choosing an antiseptic solution.

Overall, this study provides valuable insights into the effectiveness of cutaneous/mucosal antiseptics in a controlled environment, which can inform clinical practices in similar scenarios.
